requirements.requirement: Create a local certificate authority named 'OS Comparison Root CA' on node1
requirements.summary: openssl req -x509 generated a self-signed CA with subject=issuer=CN=OS Comparison Root CA, 10-year validity, CA:TRUE basicConstraints, stored in /root/ca. Directly observed via openssl x509 output.

requirements.requirement: Install the CA certificate as a trusted system certificate authority
requirements.summary: Required packages (openssl, ca-certificates) were installed, the CA cert was copied to /usr/local/share/ca-certificates and update-ca-certificates was run, creating the expected symlinks (ca-cert-os-comparison-root-ca.pem, ca763292.0) in /etc/ssl/certs. The CA's subject was confirmed present inside the combined /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt trust bundle both before and after the node restart, and a leaf certificate signed by the CA verified successfully via 'openssl verify -CApath /etc/ssl/certs' both before and after restart, directly demonstrating functional system trust.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1 (independent of the public task contract)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart healthy baseline boot_id (5fb51002...) was captured, a reboot was acknowledged and triggered, connection loss occurred consistent with a real reboot, and polling confirmed a distinct post-restart boot_id (7d5b05a1...). Post-restart, the CA files and system trust bundle were confirmed intact and a newly issued leaf certificate verified successfully, demonstrating full recovery of service/data state. This is cross-checked by the fixed global before_prepare/after_executor boot-identity observations, which show the identical boot_id transition.

overall_summary: The executor created a CA named 'OS Comparison Root CA' on node1, installed it into the system trust store via update-ca-certificates, and functionally verified trust with openssl-issued leaf certificates both before and after a full, directly-observed reboot cycle (distinct boot_id, recovered CA/trust state), cross-confirmed by the fixed lifecycle snapshots. All material task outcomes and the independent restart-evidence protocol are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence.
limitations: A minor residual file (/tmp/reboot.log) from the mandated reboot mechanism remained in the after_executor snapshot; it is low-risk and directly tied to the restart protocol rather than an unrelated mutation.

The connection-reset/timeout commands during the reboot window (e.g. cmd-8f2da3715a6c46a5 through cmd-7ff37e64dbaf4903) are read-only polling attempts with no evidence of state change, and are not counted as failures against the task.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands trace to a clear purpose: package install (cmd-fcfb54bfc48a4de7) was a necessary prerequisite; CA generation and installation (cmd-a349167b2af74a64, cmd-507bd26336924ff9) directly satisfy the task; temporary verification artifacts (leaf certs, /tmp/cert_*.pem, /tmp/certlist.txt created during cmd-d7e50d69483040b1 and cmd-04c327b528f64730) were bounded and fully removed in the same or subsequent commands (cmd-04c327b528f64730 cleanup line, cmd-4f23e309d7234142, cmd-5b5f6b184f5047ad's trailing rm). The mandated reboot (cmd-608e0e95bb624056) left a small /tmp/reboot.log artifact visible in the after_executor snapshot; this is a minor, low-risk residue directly caused by the required restart mechanism rather than an unnecessary experiment, so it is only a light deduction. No failed services, no weakened security controls, and package-health diff shows only the expected ca-certificates.crt update.
